name: Sore Loser
why: Catch-up swipe at the leader at round end; the leader can see it coming but it lands as a dull consolation, not a highlight.

name: Walk-In
why: Blind top-card recruit is a little lottery moment, and every rival gets a red as a gift.

name: Loyalists
why: Passive protection; solid but nothing happens when you play it.

name: Trendsetters
why: Shop churn on every recruit; useful, mild.

name: Spoilsport
why: Wipes out a contest someone earned all round, after play ends, with no way to answer; the leader feels robbed.

name: Body Snatchers
why: Swap at round start costs the rival a member, but they get one of the same cost back; fair enough.

name: Lie Low
why: Small steal plus a round of safety; fine.

name: Heist
why: Taking 3 followers stings one rival, but it is a visible space and a known risk.

name: Echo
why: Reading the table and copying the best previous action is a clever, satisfying play.

name: Shoplifter
why: A trickle of 1-resource steals; fine.

name: Panel
why: Upgrade or reshuffle one of your own members; fine but fiddly.

name: Demote
why: Rival loses a member but gets a pricier one back; ok trade, mild sting.

name: Doormen
why: Every round a rival loses a member you pick and gets handed one you pick (even Old Maid); they feel robbed before round III.

name: Agents
why: Quiet copy-blocker; fine.

name: Potluck
why: Rivals pick what to give and come out ahead on silver; a gift that also helps you.

name: Mob
why: Big round-end follower payout for leading red is a strong owner moment.

name: Philanthropist
why: Generous gift that pays you followers; everyone smiles.

name: Sample
why: Borrowing a rival's On Recruit is neat but usually small.

name: Old Maid
why: Nobody wants to own it; it exists to be dumped on a rival for -5 followers, which feels like being robbed.

name: Raiders
why: Once-a-game 4-follower steal, softened by paying the victim 2 white.

name: Crunch Time
why: Two turns in a row lets you string a combo; fun to pull off.

name: Debt Collectors
why: Once-a-game 2 silver from each rival; spread thin, shrug-off sting.

name: Grifter
why: Steal scaled to cult size; fine.

name: Farewell
why: Cashing out a member for followers; fine.

name: Bury
why: Shop denial plus some blue; fine.

name: High Society
why: Quiet income when rivals go silver; fine.

name: Spree
why: Three recruits in one turn is a big, fun splurge.

name: Fan Club
why: Riding the leader's best action is a satisfying catch-up moment.

name: Overtime
why: An extra minion this round always feels great.

name: Tribute Band
why: Doing every action a rival took is a huge payoff turn; the rival loses nothing.

name: Window Shopper
why: Shop churn with a little income; fine.

name: Early Birds
why: Skip-proof; quiet protection.

name: Impersonator
why: Borrowing the best rival ability and re-picking each round is a fun puzzle.

name: Window Dressers
why: Clear the shop once; fine.

name: Largesse
why: Big gift to rivals that pays you; a happy table.

name: Party Crasher
why: Sliding onto a space a rival already took is a sly, fun moment.

name: Leaders' Tax
why: Income scaled by where rivals sit; fine.

name: Poach
why: Taking a rival's member stings, but it is a round III space and expected.

name: Martyrs
why: Turns rival theft into followers; a moment the owner enjoys when it leaves.

name: Mentor & Protégés
why: A free extra recruit on arrival feels great.

name: Help Yourself
why: A spread-out resource steal; the hit is shrugged off.

name: Meddler
why: One-for-one resource swaps are a mild nuisance; fine.

name: Line Cutters
why: Going first is useful but quiet.

name: Creditor
why: Each round a rival is picked to hand over 2 followers, but they get 3 silver back; a fair-ish trade.

name: Bouncers
why: Skipping two rivals' turns is a fun jolt for you, a visible, one-time sting for them.

name: Customs Officer
why: Small consolation when robbed; fine.

name: Savings
why: Income plus one shop dig; fine.

name: Cutpurse
why: Small steal from the richest each round; shrug-off.

name: Double Agent
why: You take the member a rival built around before round III and leave them a 1-follower card they didn't pick; feels robbed.

name: Guest of Honor
why: Giving a rival a cheap member for 4 followers is a gift both sides like.

name: Debutantes
why: Doubling your silver is a big moment, and rivals get silver too.

name: Night Watch
why: Payout when rivals take Goes Last; fine.

name: Accomplice
why: A one-time 3-resource steal; fine.

name: Scavenger
why: Sniping members rivals send away is a fun, sharp moment.

name: Last Call
why: Solid late-round action; fine.

name: Toast
why: Big silver for you and a gift to everyone.

name: Initiation
why: A free recruit up to 8 is a great round III pay-off.

name: Godparent
why: Hand-off for followers; usually a gift to the rival, fine.

name: Deprogrammers
why: Adds a follower loss on top of taking a member; mild extra sting.

name: Right Away
why: Back-to-back turn; fine.

name: Hostesses
why: Steady gifts to rivals that pay you; pleasant all round.

name: Fence
why: Turns being robbed into magenta; you shrug off steals.

name: Con Men
why: Big one-time steal, usually split; fine.

name: Extortionist
why: Regular steal from the richest; a visible, shrug-off tax on the leader.

name: Closer
why: Bonus for placing last; fine.

name: Hot Streak
why: Cashing a run of turns into a burst of followers is a fun combo payoff.

name: Second-Story Man
why: Late steal can swing a contest; a sting, but known and expected.

name: Bodyguards
why: Steal immunity; quiet.

name: Tryout
why: Using a shop member's On Recruit without buying it is a clever, fun trick.

name: Night Owls
why: An extra minion from round II; fine.

name: Housewarming
why: A free member of a new color is a satisfying gain.
